en: to be quite pretty; to be lovely

examples.en: That child has a really pretty face.
A cute little cafe opened in the alley.
My sister put on neat, pretty makeup and went out.
The packaging is pretty, so it is good for gifts.
The doll that used to be so pretty has become worn out.
The house was small but pretty.

explain: '예쁘다'보다 가볍게 '제법 예쁘다'는 느낌으로 써요. 얼굴, 작은 물건, 가게에 잘 어울려요. 윗사람의 외모에는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.

phrases.en: A child with a pretty face is smiling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '예쁘장하다'를 꾸미는 말로 바꾼 형태이고 얼굴과 자주 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, which pairs often with 'face'.

phrases.en: This cup is small and rather pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 물건이 제법 예쁠 때 해요체로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite form for a small item that is quite pretty.

phrases.en: That child is quite pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 생김새를 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to casually describe how a person looks.

explain_en: It feels lighter than '예쁘다', meaning 'quite pretty'. It suits faces, small objects and shops. It's better not to use it about the looks of someone older or higher in status.

examples.ko: 이 집은 외풍이 심해서 겨울에 추워요.
examples.en: This house is very drafty, so it's cold in winter.
I stuck plastic on the window to block the draft.
Because of the draft, my nose gets cold at night.
It's an old house, so drafts come in.
There are drafts and the heating bill is high too.
Drafts come in through gaps in doors or windows.

explain: 집 안으로 들어오는 찬 바람을 말하고, 주로 문틈이나 창틈에서 들어와요. '외풍이 심하다', '외풍을 막다'처럼 자주 써요. 겨울에 오래된 집 이야기를 할 때 많이 나와요.

phrases.example: 이 방은 외풍이 심해서 잠을 잘 못 자요.
phrases.en: This room is so drafty that I can't sleep well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찬 바람이 많이 들어올 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say a place has a lot of cold drafts.

phrases.en: I blocked the gap in the door to stop the draft.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찬 바람이 들어오지 않게 무언가 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you do something to keep cold air out.

phrases.en: A draft comes in from the window side.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찬 바람이 어디로 들어오는지 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain where the cold draft is coming in from.

explain_en: Cold air seeping into a room through gaps. It means cold air coming into a house, mostly through gaps in doors or windows. People often say '외풍이 심하다' (very drafty) and '외풍을 막다' (block drafts). It comes up a lot when talking about old houses in winter.

t90.ax: It's an old house, so drafts come in.

examples.ko: 남편은 잠버릇이 나빠서 자꾸 이불을 걷어차요.
examples.en: My husband has a bad sleeping habit and keeps kicking off the blanket.

examples.ko: 제 잠버릇은 잘 때 이를 가는 거래요.
examples.en: They say my sleeping habit is grinding my teeth.

examples.ko: 아이의 잠버릇 때문에 침대 가장자리에 쿠션을 놓았어요.
examples.en: Because of my child's sleeping habits, I put cushions at the bed's edge.

examples.ko: 룸메이트의 잠버릇을 알고 나서 귀마개를 샀어요.
examples.en: After learning my roommate's sleeping habits, I bought earplugs.
I asked my family about my sleeping habits.
Even the way he sleeps is just like his dad's.

explain: 잠잘 때 나오는 습관을 말해요. '잠버릇이 나쁘다/고약하다/심하다'처럼 문제가 되는 습관을 말할 때 많이 써요. '이를 갈다', '이불을 걷어차다', '잠꼬대를 하다'가 대표적인 잠버릇이에요.

phrases.en: I'm sorry, my sleeping habits are bad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남에게 불편을 주는 잠버릇을 말할 때 가장 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common way to talk about a sleeping habit that bothers others.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a bad sleeping habit

phrases.example: 동생은 잠버릇이 심해서 같이 자기 힘들어요.
phrases.en: My brother's sleeping habits are so bad that it's hard to sleep next to him.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠버릇이 정도가 지나칠 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when a sleeping habit is extreme.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a severe sleeping habit

phrases.en: I want to fix my sleeping habit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 잠버릇을 바꾸고 싶다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you want to change a bad sleeping habit.

explain_en: Things one does in sleep, like tossing or snoring (제 친구는 잠버릇이 나빠서 자다가 이불을 자주 걷어차요.) It refers to habits that show up while sleeping. It is often used for problem habits, as in '잠버릇이 나쁘다/고약하다/심하다'. Typical examples are '이를 갈다' (grind teeth), '이불을 걷어차다' (kick off the blanket) and '잠꼬대를 하다' (talk in one's sleep).

examples.en: Do not be jealous of your friend's success.
My younger sibling was jealous of me and sulked.

examples.ko: 그는 여자 친구가 다른 남자와 이야기하면 질투해요.
examples.en: He gets jealous when his girlfriend talks to another man.

examples.ko: 질투하는 마음이 들 때는 잠깐 쉬어요.
examples.en: When I feel jealous, I take a short break.
Children sometimes feel jealous of a younger sibling.
I envied them so much that I felt jealous.

explain: 연인 사이의 질투뿐 아니라 남이 가진 것이나 잘된 일을 샘낼 때도 써요. '부러워하다'는 나쁜 마음이 없을 수도 있지만 '질투하다'는 시기하는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: I felt jealous because my friend got praised.
phrases.nuance_ko: 질투하는 마음이 생길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the feeling of jealousy arises.

phrases.en: It was hard to hide my jealous feelings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음 자체를 말할 때 '-는'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the feeling itself with -는.

phrases.en: I don't envy other people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 질투하지 않는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you don't feel jealous.

explain_en: It covers jealousy between lovers, and also resentment of what others have or how well they are doing. '부러워하다' (to envy admiringly) may carry no bad feeling, while '질투하다' has a grudging tone.

examples.en: My deskmate is very tall.
I did the homework together with my deskmate.
I am happy to have a new deskmate.
I borrowed an eraser from my deskmate.
The teacher chose our deskmates by drawing lots.

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 짝꿍이랑 계속 이야기해서 혼났어요.
examples.en: I got scolded for talking with my deskmate all through class.

explain: 학교에서 옆자리에 앉은 친구를 말해서 초등학생이 특히 많이 써요. 어른들끼리는 보통 '짝'이나 '단짝'이라고 하고, '짝꿍'은 친한 친구나 파트너를 귀엽게 부를 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I got a new seatmate today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '짝꿍'보다 덜 귀엽고, 어른들도 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less cute than 짝꿍 and also used by adults.

phrases.en: Minsu is my best buddy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옆자리가 아니어도 가장 친한 친구를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a very close friend, not necessarily one sitting next to you.

phrases.en: I became Minsu's seatmate this new semester.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자리를 정해서 옆에 앉게 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when seats are assigned and you sit next to someone.

explain_en: Friendly word for a seat partner or buddy, child-like feel. It means the classmate who sits next to you, and elementary students use it a lot. Adults usually say '짝' or '단짝', though '짝꿍' can also affectionately mean a close friend or partner.

en: to get a job; to be hired; to be employed

examples.en: My older brother finally got a job at a big company.
If you prepare hard, you will surely get hired.
My older sister got a job in Seoul and moved.
I counted the days until I would get a job.

examples.ko: 병원에 취직되면 월급을 모아서 여행을 갈래요.
examples.en: If I get hired at the hospital, I will save my pay and travel.

examples.ko: 아는 선배가 취직된 회사에 저도 지원했어요.
examples.en: I also applied to the company where a senior I know got hired.

explain: 취직하다는 내가 일자리를 얻는 행동이고, 취직되다는 합격해서 일하게 된 결과에 초점이 있어요. 그래서 구직 과정은 '취직을 준비하다', 결과는 '취직이 됐다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I got a job at a bank last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내가 일자리를 얻는 행동에 초점이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Focuses on the action of getting a job yourself.

phrases.en: My friend finally got a job.
phrases.nuance_ko: '취직되다'와 같은 뜻인데 '이/가 되다'로 결과를 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 취직되다, with 이/가 되다 stressing the result.

phrases.en: I haven't found a job yet, so I'm worried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일자리를 못 구했을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you have not been able to find a job.
phrases.en_equiv: to be unable to get a job

explain_en: Passive, result-focused; someone got hired (큰 회사에 취직되다) 취직하다 is the act of getting a job yourself, while 취직되다 focuses on the result of being accepted and starting work. So the process is '취직을 준비하다' and the result is '취직이 됐다'.

t90.ax: I counted the days until I would get a job.

examples.en: In spring, tulips bloomed fully in the park.
I gave my mother red tulips as a gift.
Tulips come in many colors, so the flower bed is colorful.
We took a family photo in front of the tulip field.

examples.ko: 튤립과 장미 중에 뭐가 더 좋아요?
examples.en: Which do you like more, tulips or roses?
The Netherlands is a country famous for tulips.

explain: '튤립이 피다'처럼 꽃이 필 때는 '피다'를 써요. 꽃을 세는 단위는 '송이'여서 '튤립 한 송이'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: When April comes, tulips bloom in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이 필 때는 '피다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '피다' is the verb for flowers blooming.

phrases.en: I put one tulip in the vase.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃은 '송이'로 세요. '튤립 두 송이'처럼 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Flowers are counted with '송이': '튤립 두 송이'.

phrases.en: I gave my friend a bouquet of tulips on her birthday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 송이를 묶은 것은 '꽃다발'이에요. 선물을 할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A bunch of flowers tied together is a '꽃다발'; common for gifts.

explain_en: For blooming, say '튤립이 피다' with '피다'. Flowers are counted with '송이', as in '튤립 한 송이'.

examples.ko: 아이가 한군데 가만히 앉아 있지를 못해요.
examples.en: The child can't sit still in one place.
Please gather the luggage in one place.
I'll stop by just one more place and then go home.
This piece of clothing is torn in one spot.

examples.ko: 한군데서 오래 일하는 게 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It isn't easy to work in one place for a long time.
This weekend I have no plans anywhere.

explain: '한 곳'과 뜻은 비슷하지만 '한군데'는 말할 때 더 편하게 붙여서 써요. '한군데도 없다'처럼 뒤에 '없다'가 오면 '한 곳도 없다'는 강한 부정이 돼요.

phrases.example: 이 방에는 깨끗한 곳이 한군데도 없어요.
phrases.en: There is not a single clean spot in this room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '없다'와 함께 쓰면 '하나도 없다'는 강한 부정이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 없다 it strongly means 'not even one'.

phrases.en: Everyone gathers in one place tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이나 물건이 한곳에 모일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when people or things gather in one place.

phrases.en: Please keep the keys in one place.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 정해진 한곳에 놓으라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when telling someone to put things in one fixed place.

explain_en: It means about the same as '한 곳', but '한군데' is written as one word and feels more casual in speech. With '없다' after it, as in '한군데도 없다', it gives a strong negative: not even one place.

en: to be discounted; to be reduced

examples.ko: 이 가방은 오늘만 삼십 퍼센트 할인돼요.
examples.en: This bag is thirty percent off today only.
All shoes were discounted during the sale.

examples.ko: 쿠폰을 쓰면 값이 더 할인될 거예요.
examples.en: If you use a coupon, the price will be reduced even more.
I picked and bought only the items on discount.
How much is taken off if I pay with this card?

examples.ko: 주말에는 이 가게 가격이 할인되지 않아요.
examples.en: Prices at this shop are not discounted on weekends.

explain: '할인하다'는 가게가 값을 깎아 주는 쪽이고, '할인되다'는 물건이나 값이 깎이는 쪽에서 말해요. 그래서 '가게가 할인해요', '값이 할인돼요'처럼 주어가 달라져요. 입말에서는 '싸지다', '깎아 주다'도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Clothes got a lot cheaper because of the sale.
phrases.nuance_ko: '할인되다'보다 편한 입말이고 값이 내려갔다는 결과만 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: More casual than 'halin-doeda', and only states that the price went down.

phrases.en: The price is reduced if you use a coupon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 값이 줄어드는 것을 말하고, 쿠폰이나 흥정 이야기에서 잘 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a price going down, often with coupons or bargaining.

phrases.en: I got a ten percent discount because I'm a student.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 주어이고 값을 깎아 주는 혜택을 받았다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The person is the subject and receives a discount.

explain_en: '할인하다' has the shop as the subject (it gives the discount), while '할인되다' has the item or price as the subject (it gets reduced). In casual speech people also say '깎아 주다' (give a cut) or '싸지다' (get cheaper).

examples.en: This shop only accepts cash.
I had no cash, so I paid by card.
If you pay in cash, I'll give you a small discount.

examples.ko: 현찰은 잃어버릴까 봐 조금만 가지고 다녀요.
examples.en: I only carry a little cash in case I lose it.
I went to the bank and withdrew cash.

examples.ko: 요즘은 현찰 없이도 지하철을 탈 수 있어요.
examples.en: These days you can ride the subway without cash.

explain: '현금'과 같은 뜻이고, '현찰'은 말할 때 더 편하게 써요. 카드나 계좌이체의 반대로 눈앞에서 내는 돈을 말해요. '현찰로 내다', '현찰만 받다'처럼 가게에서 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: If I have cash, I'll pay.
phrases.nuance_ko: '현찰'과 같은 뜻이고, 더 일반적이고 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 현찰, but more general and formal.

phrases.en: I'll pay in cash today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 카드 대신 돈으로 낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when paying with money instead of a card.

phrases.en: I don't have cash right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가진 돈이 없을 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when you have no cash on hand.

explain_en: Spoken, everyday; physical money, often at small shops. It means the same as '현금', but '현찰' sounds more casual in speech. It stands against cards or bank transfers and means money handed over on the spot. You often hear it in shops, as in '현찰로 내다' or '현찰만 받다'.

en: to refund; to give money back

examples.ko: 고장 난 물건은 가게에서 환불해 줘요.
examples.en: The shop gives refunds for broken items.
I returned the bag I bought yesterday for a refund.
It's hard to get a refund without a receipt.
Where do I go to get a refund?
The shop refunded my money.
The refund period is one week.

explain: '환불'은 돈을 돌려받는 것이고 '교환'은 다른 물건으로 바꾸는 것이에요. 물건을 돌려보내는 건 '반품하다'라서 보통 '반품하고 환불받다' 순서로 말해요. 손님은 '환불받다', 가게는 '환불해 주다'라고 말하는 게 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I got a refund for the broken bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손님이 돈을 돌려받는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the customer's side, receiving the money back.

phrases.en: Please refund this item.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에 환불을 부탁할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask a shop for a refund.

phrases.en: Sale items can't be refunded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환불할 수 없다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a refund is not possible.

explain_en: To return money for a purchase; shops and customer service. 환불 means getting money back, while '교환' means swapping for another item. Sending the goods back is '반품하다', so people often say '반품하고 환불받다' in that order. It sounds natural for the customer to say '환불받다' and for the shop to say '환불해 주다'.
